anomalies.observed: In the 'Water Level Sensor/Switches' section, R6 (10k) is wired between +3V3 and FLOAT_HIGH, and R9 (10k) is wired between GND and FLOAT_LOW. FLOAT_LOW is also tied through R2 (4k7) to the base of T1 (BT3904), the level shifter that drives the main pump FET T2.
anomalies.expected: The specification's reference netlist states the opposite pairing: 'R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k' (pull-up on the low-level float) and 'R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k'. With a pull-up on FLOAT_LOW, the float switch (to GND) can assert the line and, via R2, pull T1's base low to interlock the pump off on low water.

evidence.quote: pull resistors visible in the .cir file: R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k, R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k, R2 FLOAT_LOW /BPUMP 4.7k (design spec §4.4)
Sheet 1, water-level block: R6 10k between +3V3 and the FLOAT_HIGH label; R9 10k between the FLOAT_LOW label and GND; R2 4k7 between FLOAT_LOW and T1 base (BT3904).

anomalies.impact: FLOAT_LOW is held at GND by R9, so the low-level float switch (closing to GND) can never assert the signal, and the R2/T1 hardware pump-cutoff interlock is defeated: the main circulation pump can be enabled while the reservoir is low, allowing dry-run damage.

anomalies.observed: R5 (10k) pulls the base node of T1 (BT3904, main-pump level shifter) up to +3V3, so T1/T2 (IRLR2905) conduct whenever the PUMP_MAIN GPIO is floating or low. The parallel ATO-valve driver uses the opposite convention: R12 (10k) pulls T4's base down to GND.
anomalies.expected: Standard practice (and the matching valve-driver pattern in this same drawing) is a base pull-down resistor so the pump load is de-energized by default; the spec describes T2 as a GPIO-controlled switch ('gate driven through R1 ... pre-driven via T1') with no pull-up to the supply.

evidence.quote: Sheet 1, 'Main Pump': R5 10k between +3V3 and the green base node of T1 (which also connects R1 100R from PUMP_MAIN and R2 4k7); 'ATO Valve': R12 10k between GND and T4 base.
T2 — IRLR2905 ... gate driven through R1 (100 Ω) from the ESP32 pin, pre-driven via T1 (BT3904 NPN level shifter) (design spec §2)

anomalies.impact: The main circulation pump energizes at power-up and whenever the MCU pin is not actively driven low, instead of defaulting off; combined with the defeated low-float interlock this removes the safe-state behavior of the pump output.
